description: Reads a NONMEM CSV file, recognises the reserved columns (ID, TIME, DV, AMT, EVID, MDV, CMT...), converts '.' to missing values, computes the relative time, the time after dose (TAD) and the dose-normalised DV, and flags BLQ records.
code:
dat <- nm_read_csv(
  file.path(ex, "example_data.csv")   # file: path of the NONMEM CSV data set
)
head(dat$data)     # standardised data (reserved NONMEM names)
dat$mapping        # reserved labels -> original column names

description: Number of subjects, records and observations, proportion of BLQ, time range, distinct doses and observed compartments.
Observed concentrations against TIME or TAD, with the median and an interval band, on linear and/or log scale, optionally stratified by a covariate.
code:
nm_plot_dv(dat$data,          # data: data frame from nm_read_csv()
           scales = "both")   # y axis: "linear", "log" or "both" (side by side)
nm_plot_dv(dat$data,
           time_var = "TAD",  # x axis: "TIME" (default) or "TAD" (time after dose)
           scales   = "log")
nm_plot_dv(dat$data,
           y     = "DV_norm", # y: "DV" (default) or "DV_norm" (DV / dose)
           strat = "GENO")    # column used to colour the profiles

description: Reads the dataset, summarises it and draws the raw and dose-normalised profiles in one call, with configurable BLQ handling and optional JPEG/CSV export.
code:
pv <- nm_data_previsual(
  file.path(ex, "example_data.csv"),  # path of the CSV data set
  scales    = "both",                 # y axis: "linear", "log" or "both"
  dose_norm = TRUE                    # also plot DV_norm = DV / AMT
)
pv$summary     # summary table
pv$plot_dv     # concentrations vs time
pv$plot_norm   # dose-normalised concentrations

description: Adds a RATE column (e.g. -2 for an estimated zero-order duration) on all doses or only on some routes, keeping the exact format of the file.
code:
# writes example_data_rate.csv next to the source file
nm_add_rate(
  file.path(ex, "example_data.csv"),  # file: path of the original CSV
  dose_value = -2                     # RATE on doses: -2 (duration estimated)
)                                     #   or -1 (rate estimated)

description: Writes a data.frame as CSV with the NONMEM convention for missing values ('.').
code:
nm_export_data(
  dat$data,                       # data: data frame to write
  file.path(ex, "data_nm.csv")    # file: output path (folder created if needed)
)

description: Checks that a dataset can be read by NONMEM: missing ID or TIME, non-increasing times, inconsistent EVID/MDV/AMT, duplicates, non-numeric columns, outliers.

task: Suggest a structural model and initial values
description: Analyses the data before any NONMEM run and ranks candidate models (compartments, input, elimination, residual error), each with initial values for THETA, IIV and SIGMA and alerts on what no candidate describes.
code:
s <- nm_suggest_model(
  file.path(ex, "example_data.csv")   # data: path of the CSV (or a data frame)
)
s                  # ranked candidates, initial values, alerts
plot(s, "profiles")   # type: "profiles", "support", "pooled" or "design"
plot(s, "support")

description: Expected RSE of the parameters and eta-shrinkage of a candidate for the sampling design of the dataset or for another design, from the population Fisher information matrix.
code:
nm_suggest_design(s,              # s: result of nm_suggest_model()
                  candidate = 1)  # candidate number (default 1)
# sparse design: 3 samples, 100 subjects
nm_suggest_design(s,
                  times      = c(1, 4, 12),  # sampling times after the dose
                  n_subjects = 100)          # number of subjects

description: Writes the control streams of the chosen candidates, runs them with nm_run(), reads their OFV and ranks them by BIC.
code:
r <- nm_suggest_run(
  s,                     # result of nm_suggest_model()
  analysis_dir = ex,     # folder where the control streams are written and run
  nmfe_path    = nmfe,   # path of the nmfe launcher
  candidates   = 1:3,    # candidate numbers to run (default: the first 3)
  n_cores      = 3       # number of runs at the same time
)
r                        # OFV, BIC, ranks, Spearman correlation

description: Compares the individual estimates (CL, central volume, absorption) between covariate groups with the Wasserstein distance, before any modelling.
code:
nm_suggest_covariates(
  s,                            # result of nm_suggest_model()
  covariates = c("WT", "GENO")  # covariate columns of the data set
)

description: Writes a complete control stream for a compartmental PK model (1 to 3 compartments, IV or extravascular, first-order, zero-order or transit absorption, linear or Michaelis-Menten elimination), possibly from a candidate of nm_suggest_model().
code:
# from candidate 1 of a suggestion
nm_write_ctl(file.path(ex, "run3.ctl"),  # file: control stream to write
             from      = s,              # result of nm_suggest_model()
             candidate = 1)              # candidate number in `from`
# or from the dataset columns
nm_write_ctl(input = file.path(ex, "example_data.csv"),  # data set (or its column names)
             error = "combined")   # "additive", "proportional" or "combined"

description: Checks a control stream without NM-TRAN: THETA, ETA and EPS used without declaration, items missing from $INPUT, M3 requirements; optional line differences from a reference.
code:
nm_ctl_check(
  file.path(ex, "run2.ctl")   # ctl: control stream (path or lines)
)
ctl <- nm_write_ctl(input = file.path(ex, "example_data.csv"))
nm_ctl_check(nm_ctl_mu(ctl),     # ctl: the transformed control stream
             reference = ctl)    # original: line differences are added

description: Rewrites log-normal parameters as MU_m = LOG(THETA(n)) and P = EXP(MU_m + ETA(m)), as required by EM and Bayesian methods (SAEM, IMP, BAYES).
code:
ctl <- nm_write_ctl(input = file.path(ex, "example_data.csv"),
                    error = "combined")
nm_ctl_mu(ctl)       # ctl: control stream (path or lines); all parameters
nm_ctl_mu(ctl,
          parameters = c("CL", "V"),  # parameters to transform
          mode       = "linear")      # "readable" (default) or "linear"

description: Adds IOV to chosen parameters with $ABBR REPLACE and $OMEGA BLOCK SAME; the occasion item must be in $INPUT.
code:
cols <- c("ID", "TIME", "AMT", "DV", "EVID", "MDV", "CMT", "OCC", "BQL")
ctl  <- nm_write_ctl(input = cols,         # column names of the data set
                     error = "combined")
nm_ctl_iov(ctl,
           parameters = c("CL", "V"),  # parameters receiving IOV
           n_occ      = 3,             # number of occasions (at least 2)
           occ        = "OCC")         # occasion column, values 1 to n_occ

description: Applies the M3 method (Beal 2001): BLQ observations contribute P(DV < LLOQ); the LLOQ is a constant, a dataset column or depends on the analytical method.
code:
cols <- c("ID", "TIME", "AMT", "DV", "EVID", "MDV", "CMT", "OCC", "BQL")
ctl  <- nm_write_ctl(input = cols, error = "combined")
nm_ctl_m3(ctl,
          bql  = "BQL",   # BQL flag column (0 = quantified, 1 = below LLOQ)
          lloq = 0.02)    # LLOQ, on the DV scale

task: Convert a Wings label control stream
description: Converts a Wings for NONMEM 'extended' control stream, where the model uses the parameter labels, into a standard one (THETA(n), ETA(n), ERR(n)).
code:
# a Wings control stream of your own (not in the example project)
nm_convert_ctl(
  "C:/myproject/run_wings.ctl"   # ctl: Wings control stream with labels
)                                # -> run_wings_converted.ctl

description: Runs control streams with nmfe, without Wings or PsN, each in its own run directory; finished runs are skipped. n_cores runs several models at the same time.
code:
log <- nm_run(
  ctl          = c("run1.ctl", "run2.ctl"),  # control streams (relative to analysis_dir)
  nmfe_path    = nmfe,                       # path of the nmfe launcher
  analysis_dir = ex,                         # analysis folder (one subfolder per run)
  n_cores      = 2                           # runs at the same time ("auto", "ask")
)
log[, c("run", "action", "ofv", "min_ok", "cov_status")]

description: Logical and physical cores of the computer and the number of simultaneous runs used by n_cores = "auto".
code: nm_cores()   # no argument: logical and physical cores of this computer

task: Summarise all runs of a project
description: Reads every run of an analysis folder: OFV, dOFV, AIC/BIC, minimisation and covariance status, warnings, and all parameters named from the model code (CL, V, KA...).
code:
runs <- nm_extract_runs(
  ex      # path: analysis folder (or the folder of a single run)
)
runs      # one line per run
nm_filter_runs(runs,           # x: result of nm_extract_runs()
               "successful")$runs   # filter: "all", "successful",
                                    #   "successful_no_warning", "clean"...

description: One row per parameter and one column per run, aligned by name or by NONMEM index; values, RSE, SE or shrinkage.
code:
nm_compare_runs(runs,           # result of nm_extract_runs()
                format = TRUE)  # cells written "value (RSE%)"
nm_compare_runs(runs,
                what = "shrinkage")   # "value", "rse_pct", "se" or "shrinkage"

description: Parameter table of a run (estimates, SE, RSE, 95% CI, SD of ETAs and EPS, ETA correlations) exported to a Word document in the run directory.
code:
res <- nm_extract_run_table(
  file.path(ex, "run2.reg")   # run: run folder, control stream or stem
)
res$params          # the table in R
res$output_file     # the Word file

task: Identify the role of THETAs and ETAs
description: Reads $PK or $PRED and links each THETA and ETA to the PK parameter it acts on, with its role (typical value, covariate effect, IIV, residual error).
code:
x <- nm_identify_parameters(
  file.path(ex, "run2.ctl")   # ctl: path of the control stream
)
x$parameter_table
nm_identify_directory(ex)     # path: every control stream of a folder

description: Summary table of all runs of a project exported to Word (today nm_extract_runs() gives it in R only).
Tree of the runs with, for each, its parent run, OFV, dOFV against the parent and convergence status. Parents are read from the ";; Based on:" comments of the control streams, or given with parents.
code:
d <- nm_model_diagram(
  ex,                         # x: analysis folder (or nm_extract_runs() result)
  parents = c(run2 = "run1")  # optional links run = parent, added to (or
)                             #   replacing) the ";; Based on:" comments
d                       # table of the runs
plot(d)                 # the diagram

description: Standard diagnostic plots from a NONMEM table: observations vs population and individual predictions, CWRES, NPDE and IWRES vs time and predictions.
code:
gof <- nm_gof(
  file.path(ex, "run2.reg")   # file: run folder, or the NONMEM table itself
)
plot(gof)
nm_gof(file.path(ex, "run2.reg"),
       by = "GENO")           # columns used to split the plots into panels

task: Compare two models (LRT, Vuong, Clarke, bootstrap, influence)
description: Paired comparison of two runs: CWRES and NPDE, individual OFVs, Vuong and Clarke tests for non-nested models, LRT if nested, subject bootstrap of dOFV, influence, paired parameters and ETAs; summary() gives a decision grid.
code:
cmp <- nm_compare(
  file.path(ex, "run1.reg"),      # run1: first run (folder or path prefix)
  file.path(ex, "run2.reg"),      # run2: second run
  labels     = c("Base", "Final"),   # display names of the two runs
  covariates = c("WT", "GENO")       # covariates examined against the
)                                    #   per-subject difference of iOFV
summary(cmp)            # decision grid
cmp$tests$table

description: Where the second model improves or degrades the fit (gain map with bootstrap band), diagnostics of both runs overlaid, caterpillar of individual dOFV, parameters and ETAs.
code:
plot(cmp,                  # result of nm_compare()
     type   = "gain_map",  # figure(s) to draw (see ?plot.nm_compare)
     n_band = 200)         # subject resamples for the confidence band
plot(cmp, type = c("overlay_gof", "iofv_caterpillar", "eta_scatter"))

task: Optimise a base model without iterative runs
description: Ranks the possible changes of a base model (residual error, random effects, covariates) by their expected dOFV, from its outputs (level 1) and one NONMEM evaluation run (level 2, linearised model).
code:
# level 1 only, no NONMEM run
nm_optimize_base(file.path(ex, "run1.reg"),      # run: base run folder
                 covariates = c("WT", "GENO"),   # covariate columns to test
                 level      = 1)                 # 1 = residual analysis only
# level 2: one evaluation run, then the linearised model
p <- nm_derivatives_ctl(file.path(ex, "run1.reg"))  # writes run1_deriv.ctl
nm_run(basename(p),   # ctl: the control stream written above
       nmfe,          # nmfe_path
       dirname(p))    # analysis_dir: the folder of that control stream
o <- nm_optimize_base(file.path(ex, "run1.reg"), covariates = c("WT", "GENO"))
o
plot(o)

description: Compares the distribution of an ETA between covariate groups with the Wasserstein distance and a permutation test, with the Wasserstein R2 between runs (Simon et al., Front Pharmacol 2026).
code:
w <- nm_wasserstein(
  c(BASE  = file.path(ex, "run1.reg"),   # runs: run folders, named
    FINAL = file.path(ex, "run2.reg")),  #   (the names label the results)
  covariates = c("WT", "GENO"),          # covariate columns compared
  eta        = "CL"                      # ETA analysed: a parameter name,
)                                        #   "ETA(n)" or an index
w
plot(w)                 # type = "ecdf" (default)
plot(w, type = "r2w")

description: Writes and runs the _orig and _sim control streams of a VPC from an estimated run, then draws observed percentiles against the confidence intervals of simulated percentiles.
code:
nm_vpc_ctl(file.path(ex, "run2.ctl"),  # run: estimation run (ctl, folder or stem)
           nmfe_path = nmfe,     # path of the nmfe launcher
           n_sim     = 500,      # number of simulated replicates
           n_cores   = 2)        # 2 = the _orig and _sim runs at the same time
cols <- c("NSIM", "ID", "TIME", "AMT", "MDV", "DV", "PRED", "IPRED")
nm_vpc(file.path(ex, "run2.ctl"),  # run: same as in nm_vpc_ctl()
       col_names = cols)           # names of the $TABLE columns of the .fit files

description: Prediction-corrected VPC (Bergstrand 2011) from the same simulation runs as the VPC.
code:
cols <- c("NSIM", "ID", "TIME", "AMT", "MDV", "DV", "PRED", "IPRED")
nm_vpc(file.path(ex, "run2.ctl"),
       col_names  = cols,   # names of the $TABLE columns of the .fit files
       type       = 2,      # 1 = VPC (default), 2 = prediction-corrected VPC
       bin_method = 3)      # 3 = nominal times (1 manual, 2 quantiles, 4 auto)

description: Non-parametric bootstrap by subject: reproducible and optionally stratified resampling, resume after interruption, percentile confidence intervals and success rate.
code:
boot <- nm_bootstrap(
  file.path(ex, "run2.reg", "run2.ctl"),  # ctl: control stream of the final model
  nmfe_path = nmfe,     # path of the nmfe launcher
  n         = 500,      # number of replicates
  seed      = 1,        # seed, for a reproducible resampling
  strata    = "GENO",   # optional column to stratify the resampling on
  n_cores   = "auto"    # replicates at the same time (physical cores - 1)
)
boot
plot(boot)

description: Leave-one-subject-out runs ranked by |dOFV|, with relative and standardised THETA shifts. A descriptive influence diagnostic, not an outlier test.
code:
jk <- nm_jackknife(
  file.path(ex, "run2.reg", "run2.ctl"),  # ctl: control stream, already run
  nmfe_path = nmfe,     # path of the nmfe launcher
  n_cores   = "auto"    # runs at the same time (physical cores - 1)
)
jk
plot(jk, "bar")         # type: "bar" (default), "rank" or "scatter"
plot(jk, "scatter")

description: Fixes a THETA at each value of a grid, re-runs the model and reads the OFV; the confidence interval is where dOFV crosses 3.84.
code:
prof <- nm_profile(
  file.path(ex, "run2.reg", "run2.ctl"),  # ctl: reference control stream
  nmfe,                  # nmfe_path: path of the nmfe launcher
  param   = "CL",        # parameter profiled: $THETA label or index
  from    = 4.6,         # grid of fixed values: first value,
  to      = 5.7,         #   last value,
  by      = 0.1,         #   and step
  n_cores = "auto"       # grid values run at the same time
)
prof
plot(prof, type = "dofv")   # "ofv" or "dofv" (with the CI threshold line)

description: Saves a ggplot to JPEG, PNG, PDF or TIFF according to the file extension, creating the folder if needed.
code:
g <- nm_plot_dv(dat$data)
nm_export_plot(g,                                       # plot: the figure
               file.path(ex, "figures", "dv_time.png"), # file: type from the extension
               width  = 8,                              # width in inches
               height = 5)                              # height in inches

description: Writes all goodness-of-fit plots of a run to a Word document next to its table.
code:
nm_gof(file.path(ex, "run2.reg"),  # file: run folder (or table)
       save_docx = TRUE)            # write all the plots to a Word file
                                    #   in the analysis folder
